studyNotes.title: Fermat & Euler Remainder Theorems: Solved CAT Benchmark Problems
studyNotes.content:
### Problem Breakdown (Solved Q&A):

#### Question:
Find the remainder when **3^{2026} + 5^{2027}** is divided by **17**.

---

### Step-by-Step Solution & Method:

#### 1. Part A: Remainder of $3^{2026} \pmod{17}$
- Since **17** is prime and $\gcd(3, 17) = 1$, apply **Fermat's Little Theorem**:
  $$a^{p-1} \equiv 1 \pmod{p} \implies 3^{16} \equiv 1 \pmod{17}$$
- Divide the exponent 2026 by 16:
  $$2026 = 16 \times 126 + 10$$
- Therefore:
  $$3^{2026} \equiv (3^{16})^{126} \times 3^{10} \equiv 1 \times 3^{10} \pmod{17}$$
- Evaluating $3^{10} \pmod{17}$:
  - $3^3 = 27 \equiv 10 \pmod{17}$
  - $3^6 = 100 \equiv 15 \equiv -2 \pmod{17}$
  - $3^{10} = 3^6 \times 3^4 = (-2) \times 81 \equiv (-2) \times 13 = -26 \equiv 8 \pmod{17}$
- **Remainder for Part A = 8**

#### 2. Part B: Remainder of $5^{2027} \pmod{17}$
- Again by Fermat's Theorem: $5^{16} \equiv 1 \pmod{17}$
- Divide 2027 by 16: $2027 = 16 \times 126 + 11$
- $5^{2027} \equiv 5^{11} \pmod{17}$
  - $5^2 = 25 \equiv 8 \pmod{17}$
  - $5^4 = 64 \equiv 13 \equiv -4 \pmod{17}$
  - $5^8 \equiv (-4)^2 = 16 \equiv -1 \pmod{17}$
  - $5^{11} = 5^8 \times 5^2 \times 5^1 \equiv (-1) \times 8 \times 5 = -40 \equiv 11 \pmod{17}$
- **Remainder for Part B = 11**

#### Final Combination:
- Total Remainder = $(8 + 11) \pmod{17} = 19 \pmod{17} = \mathbf{2}$

> **Rule for Exam:** When dividing by a prime $P$, always reduce exponent modulo $(P - 1)$ first. It cuts computation time by 80%.

studyNotes.title: Circular & Linear Arrangements: Core Deduction Matrix
studyNotes.content:
### Core Rules for Circular Arrangements (DILR):

#### 1. Directional Orientation Matrix:
| Facing | Left Movement | Right Movement | Opposite Person |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Facing Center** | Clockwise | Counter-clockwise | At $(N/2)$ positions for even $N$ |
| **Facing Away** | Counter-clockwise | Clockwise | At $(N/2)$ positions for even $N$ |

#### 2. Four Golden Rules for Set Selection & Solving:
1. **Never start with negative clues:** Skip "A does not sit next to B" initially.
2. **Anchor the absolute positions first:** Begin with clues that link at least 2 people to fixed reference points (e.g. "B sits third to the left of C").
3. **Dual-Case Branching:** If a clue leads to only 2 configurations, draw both circles immediately rather than trying to hold them in working memory.
4. **The 8-Minute Cutoff:** If 0 solid deductions are made within 8 minutes of starting a DILR set, abandon and move to the next set immediately.

studyNotes.title: Reading Comprehension: Author Tone Identification Quick Reference
studyNotes.content:
### Master Author Tone Reference Card (CAT VARC)

#### 1. Analytical & Objective Tones:
- **Detached / Objective:** Neutral presentation of facts, data, and contrasting perspectives without emotional words.
- **Expository / Informative:** Explains how a mechanism, historical event, or scientific phenomenon works.

#### 2. Critical & Skeptical Tones:
- **Acerbic / Vitriolic:** Harsh, biting criticism with stinging or contemptuous language.
- **Cynical:** Believes people or institutions act solely out of selfish motives.
- **Skeptical / Questioning:** Doubts conventional claims and demands stronger evidentiary proof.

#### 3. Praising & Supportive Tones:
- **Eulogistic / Laudatory:** High praise, admiring contributions or historical figures.
- **Reverent:** Deep respect, awe, and veneration (common in art and philosophy passages).

#### 4. Cautionary & Prescriptive Tones:
- **Didactic:** Educational tone intended to instruct morality or proper procedure.
- **Admonitory / Cautionary:** Warning of grave negative consequences if current trends persist.

> **Elimination Rule:** Extreme tones (*vitriolic, fanatical, ecstatic*) are rarely the correct answer in CAT RC unless the text is extraordinarily biased.

guideSections.title: CAT Examination Structure & Format
guideSections.contentMarkdown:
### CAT Exam Architecture & Timing
- **Total Duration:** 120 Minutes (2 Hours)
- **Sections:** 3 Sequential Sections strictly timed at **40 Minutes each** (No section jumping allowed)
- **Total Questions:** 68 Questions (49 Multiple Choice Questions + 17 Non-MCQ / TITA Questions)

#### Sectional Breakdown:
| Section Name | What it Tests | Questions | Time Limit | MCQ Count | TITA Count |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| **VARC** | English comprehension & verbal reasoning | 24 | 40 mins | 21 | 3 |
| **DILR** | Logical reasoning & data interpretation | 22 | 40 mins | 14 | 6 |
| **QA** | Mathematics & quantitative aptitude | 22 | 40 mins | 14 | 8 |
| **Total** | Full Comprehensive Test | **68** | **120 mins** | **49** | **17** |

#### Scoring Scheme:
- **+3 Marks** for every correct answer.
- **-1 Mark** for every incorrect Multiple Choice Question (MCQ).
- **0 Marks (No negative marking)** for incorrect Type-In-The-Answer (TITA) questions.

guideSections.title: Strategy for 90%+: Target Net Score Benchmarks
guideSections.contentMarkdown:
### Blueprint Target Scores for 90th Percentile+
*(Derived directly from the reference guide as bare-minimum raw score targets)*

- **VARC (Verbal Ability & Reading Comprehension):** **15 – 20** net score
- **DILR (Data Interpretation & Logical Reasoning):** **10** net score
- **QA (Quantitative Aptitude):** **5+** net score

> **Note on Strategy:** These raw score targets represent the minimum thresholds outlined in the preparation guide. Consistency across all three sections is required to clear sectional cutoffs at top IIMs and tier-1 business schools.

guideSections.title: Quantitative Aptitude (QA): Topics & 9-Step Sequence
guideSections.contentMarkdown:
### Concepts to Master:
- **Arithmetic:** Percentages, profit and loss, ratios, averages, simple and compound interest, mixtures and alligations, partnerships, time and work, speed, distance and time.
- **Algebra:** Linear equations, quadratic equations, inequalities, functions, logarithms, sequences and progressions.
- **Number System:** Divisibility, factors, multiples, HCF and LCM, remainders (Fermat, Euler, Wilson), cyclicity.
- **Geometry & Mensuration:** Triangles, circles, quadrilaterals, polygons, area, perimeter, surface area, volume, coordinate geometry, trigonometry.
- **Modern Maths:** Permutations and combinations, probability, set theory.

### Recommended 9-Step Learning Sequence:
1. **Ratio and proportion** (Base of arithmetic)
2. **Profit and loss**
3. **Simple and compound interest**
4. **Mixtures and alligations**
5. **Time and work**
6. **Time, speed and distance**
7. **Number systems**
8. **Geometry and mensuration**
9. **Modern mathematics**

guideSections.title: Data Interpretation & Logical Reasoning (DILR)
guideSections.contentMarkdown:
### Data Interpretation Topics:
- Tables and caselets, Bar graphs, Line graphs, Pie charts, Mixed graphs, Data comparison, Data sufficiency.

### Logical Reasoning Topics:
- Linear seating arrangements, Circular seating arrangements, Selection and distribution, Scheduling problems, Games and tournaments, Blood relations, Ranking and ordering, Venn diagrams, Routes and networks, Conditional logic and puzzles.

### Recommended Problem-Set Sequence:
1. Tables and charts
2. Linear arrangements
3. Circular arrangements
4. Scheduling and distribution
5. Games and tournaments
6. Mixed and advanced puzzles

> **Key Rule from Guide:** *Don't just learn formulas. DILR is primarily about practising different types of problem sets rather than rote memorization.*

guideSections.title: Verbal Ability & Reading Comprehension (VARC)
guideSections.contentMarkdown:
### Reading Comprehension (RC) Skills:
- Identify the central idea of a passage.
- Understand the author's perspective and tone.
- Identify assumptions and underlying arguments.
- Draw logical inferences (what is implied, not stated).
- Identify supporting and contradictory statements.

### Verbal Ability (VA) Question Types:
- Para jumbles (TITA - No negative marking)
- Para summaries
- Odd sentence out
- Sentence placement
- Paragraph completion

### Daily Preparation Guidelines:
- Read 1 or 2 long-form articles every day across economics, business, science, psychology, and philosophy.
- Practise reading without translating every sentence into your native language.
- Solve 2–3 reading comprehension passages regularly under untimed conditions initially, moving to timed (7–8 min/passage) in Phase 2.
- Focus on understanding the author's argument rather than memorising vocabulary.

> **Key Principle:** *Comprehension and contextual understanding are more important than memorising thousands of isolated English words.*
